edits.current: THE PER-EMPLOYEE, PER-MONTH SIDE of the ET art. 114-1 exoneration (introduced by Ley 1607 de 2012 and confirmed by Ley 1819 de 2016 art. 65). Values are S and N, not X. The employer-level flag in A1-033 declares eligibility; THIS field applies it to a specific employee in a specific month. The test is monthly, so an employee who crosses 10 SMMLV because of a bonus loses the exoneration for that month alone - the engine must evaluate it every period, never once a year. edits.proposed: THE PER-EMPLOYEE, PER-MONTH SIDE of the ET art. 114-1 exoneration (introduced by Ley 1607 de 2012 and confirmed by Ley 1819 de 2016 art. 65). Values are S and N, not X. The employer-level flag in A1-033 declares eligibility; THIS field applies it to a specific employee in a specific month. TWO RULES APPLY TOGETHER. (1) The exoneration test is on the TOTAL EARNINGS of the month (total devengado): the employee is exonerated where the total devengado of the month is below 10 SMMLV (COP 17,509,050 in 2026) - Decreto 1828 de 2013 art. 7. It is an earnings test, NOT a test on the health IBC. (2) In addition, AT2 v30 campo 76 requires N whenever the health contribution base in campo 43 (T2R2-043) is at or above 10 SMMLV. The field is therefore S only where BOTH the total devengado and the health IBC are below 10 SMMLV. The test is monthly, so an employee who crosses 10 SMMLV because of a bonus loses the exoneration for that month alone - the engine must evaluate it every period, never once a year. Where marked S, the employer's health 8.5%, SENA 2% and ICBF 3% fall away and the health rate in T2R2-054 becomes the EMPLOYEE rate alone (4%); pension, occupational risk and the CCF 4% remain payable in full. PMI evidence (Sept-2026): the client flags on an earnings figure, not on the IBC - all 88 integral-salary employees are non-exonerated, and a 'total monthly entitlements >= 10 SMMLV' test reproduces the client's flags in 233 of 241 cases, while the health-IBC test reproduces 222 of 241. No single test reproduces all 241 cases, and one employee with a health IBC above 10 SMMLV is exonerated in the client run, which rule (2) does not allow; the client's exact devengado definition is therefore to be confirmed (see Query to RA).
edits.reason: Explanation described the test only in general terms and the spec elsewhere tested the health IBC; decision 3 fixes both rules (Decreto 1828 de 2013 art. 7 and AT2 v30 campo 76); evidence counts per the verifier (222 of 241 on the IBC test, 233 of 241 on the entitlements test, 88 integral employees non-exonerated).

Report the IGE and LMA authorisation numbers (T2R2-057, T2R2-059) and values (T2R2-058, T2R2-060), and model the benefit as PAID to the employee and RECEIVABLE from the institution.
